name: list_devices
description: List all smart-home devices known to HOMEd. Each entry has the device `name` plus an optional `named_properties` array — user-defined names for individual sub-properties (set in homed-web UI). For multi-channel devices the device `name` may be generic (e.g. "Реле освещения"), while `named_properties` tells which channel is "Мастерская", "Кухня", etc. To find a device by a human phrase, call this with no filters and search the returned array yourself — it is small enough.

service.description: Optional filter by HOMEd service topic (e.g. 'zigbee').

name: get_device
description: Return full information about a single device: exposes (capabilities), options and last known property values. Pass either the canonical key ("<type>/<id>"), the device name, or the device id.

name: set_properties
description:
Publish property updates to HOMEd devices in a single batch call. Always prefer one call with many operations to many sequential calls.

One operation targets ONE (device, endpoint) pair. To know what you can write, call get_device (or list_devices with includeState=true) and inspect `exposes.<endpoint>.properties`: every entry with `writable: true` may be set, the key is the exact sub-key you put under `properties`, and `enum`/`min`/`max`/`unit`/`note` describe the accepted value. `endpoint` is the numeric exposes key — omit it for `exposes.common` (also when sub-keys carry a `_N` suffix). Group several sub-keys of the same (device, endpoint) into one operation.

If you matched the device via `named_properties`, its `endpoint` and `property` are already the values you need.

Operations are processed independently — failure on one does not abort the others.

operations.description: Array of independent updates. Each item targets ONE (device, endpoint) pair and may carry multiple sub-keys.

endpoint.description: Numeric endpoint id. Set when the items live under exposes["<N>"]. Do NOT set when items are in exposes.common.

properties.description: Map of sub-key → target value, all written to the same td/ topic in ONE message. Keys are bare (e.g. "status", "level") when `endpoint` is set OR the device is single-endpoint; they carry a _N suffix (e.g. "status_5") only when the matching item is in common with a _N suffix and `endpoint` is NOT set. Values: boolean for toggle/button, string for status/select/systemMode/etc., number for level/position/targetTemperature, array [r,g,b] for color.

name: query_history
description: Query recorded values for a (device, property) pair from homed-recorder. Returns timestamps and values (or hourly aggregates for long ranges).

start.description: Range start, Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

end.description: Range end, Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
